messages.subject: Syntax for setting data filter that excludes one of multiple categories in a field
parts:
Hi List,

I have a question similar to the one posted by Cleve Hicks on setting up data filters.  I have a field in my observation layer that refers the type of detection: visual, "a", and aural detections in three categories "b", "c", and "d" I would like run an analysis on just "a", "b", "c", by excluding category "d."  Could someone help me with syntax for this?

Thanks!
Caroline

E.g.

All Observations
"Observation (m)"   "type"
0                                a
12                              b
20                              b
10                              c
2                                d
5                                d

Data filtered for type a, b, and c
"Observation (m)"   "type"
0                                a
12                              b
20                              b
10                              c

parts:
Hi Caroline,

Maybe the simplest if you just have 4 types is to use something like ***type="a" OR type="b" OR type="c"***; that should do the trick

Many details provided in the help file under "Data Selection Tab"

hope this helps

T

messages.author: 9b03386432b784c0
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Syntax for setting data filter that excludes one of multiple categories in a field
parts:
Hi Caroline,

Without looking at it your actual analysis I wonder, are you sure you are not looking at the 3 sets of distances that distance outputs by default for an analysis of ungrouped (i.e. exact) distances? If that is the case then note that corresponds to a single analysis and the different histograms are there just for illustration purposes, and the only difference is in the GOF measures (as the chi-squared is calculated with 3 different sets of bins). It's a coincidence you had 3 types and 3 outputs.

Please correct me if I'm wrong though. One way or the other, lets do it off the list because (1) I don't want to be wrong in front of everyone else ;) and (2) let's avoid filling other people e-mail boxes with stuff that might not be relevant. If useful to others, we'll post a summary once we have sorted what was going on.

cheers,

T

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: Syntax for setting data filter that excludes one of multiple categories in a field
parts:
Just to pick up on the original data filter question.  An efficient way to frame this query is using the operator "IN", as follows:

type IN ("a","b","c")

Another alternative would be to use NOT

NOT (type = "d")

Cheers, Len

messages.author: 2205c8a4e2902bac
messages.subject: Re: Syntax for setting data filter that excludes one of multiple categories in a field
parts:
Hi Len and others: thanks for the help with framing the query! Very helpful. 

I also wanted to share what Eric explained to me in regards to my other question: why do I see three sets of results when I analyze ungrouped data? I had previously conducted analyses on only grouped data, and so was accustomed to seeing just one set of chi square results. This led me to think I had messed something up with the data filter and the program was analyzing different subsets of my data separately. That was not the case.  Eric and others have since pointed out that for ungrouped data, the program Distance will choose three different "guesses" or sets of experimental cutpoints with which to explore model fit. So in a single analysis, you should expect three sets of result pages corresponding to these three sets of experimental cutpoints.

See p. 105 (CDS: CDS Results details listing) for more information.

Eric et al., feel free to jump in here and add (or correct) any information!

Many thanks,
Caroline
